rulings.barItem: a stated cause that never happens, and a promise never kept
rulings.reason: The life's 'about' still says 'FIRST ACT ONLY ... The life grows with each act of the outline', and the outline promises LibreChat making its collections, a person signing up and in, a chat saved by findAndModify, a session deleted on sign-out. None of it happens: steps 8-223 replay spec/recordings/ one by one, each in its own throwaway database (ask_find_all, ask_insert_number_kinds, ... ask_filter_projection_dotted_include) on collections named people, things, nobody, owners; no step touches users, conversations, messages, sessions, roles or accessroles from journeys/demand.json.
rulings.correction: Rewrite the life as the outline's acts in one database on LibreChat's own collections and documents (the commands of journeys/demand.json in its phases: boot, register, login, first page, chat, conversation list and reopen, logout), and correct 'about' to say what the life is.

rulings.barItem: a feature tour: one call per option of an endpoint in a row
rulings.reason: Steps 60-93 are one find per filter operator ($eq on a string, null, number kinds, array, $exists true/false, $in, empty $in, empty $nin, $ne, $gt/$lte, $lte null, $or/$and, $type, projections), each after re-inserting the same six documents; steps 94-142 one update per option ($set, same value, multi, no match, $unset, $addToSet, upsert variants); 143-170 one findAndModify per option; 173-178 distinct, 179-188 delete with limit 1, 0 and no match, 189-195 aggregate, 202-219 listCollections variants, 220-223 projections. This is the decision table's recording list walked in order, not an application's use.
rulings.correction: Keep each command only where the story's act sends it, with the filter, update and options LibreChat sends there; delete the per-option probes.

rulings.reason: Every 'after it, X holds exactly what the server held' find and 'has exactly the indexes the server had' listIndexes (the steps listed) reads back what the step before just wrote, by the same application that holds it; no other actor reads it and nothing in the story uses the answer. Step 4 reads back the two people step 3 just wrote, again with no one needing them.
rulings.correction: Delete these read-backs; a read stays only where the application reads in the story (a sign-in finding the user, the conversation list, a conversation reopened).

rulings.barItem: a refusal without a cause the story shows; a run of refusals
rulings.reason: Step 5 sends noSuchCommand, step 36 lists the indexes of a collection never made, steps 39 and 40 send a field 'noSuchField' on find and insert: four refusals, 36-40 nearly in a row, none with a cause. LibreChat sends no unknown command and lists indexes only on agentqueuedturns after making it (journeys/demand.json), and the driver cannot send a field its builders do not have (spec/command-builders.json, read from the driver of record, spec/clients/mongodb-6.20.0.tgz (MongoDB's Node driver 6.20.0, Apache-2.0, the spec's stand-in for the vendor's documentation per spec/SOURCE.md)).

The duplicate-key refusal (E11000) is drawn nine times: steps 12, 16, 21, 47, 52, 57, 136, 207 and 212, each on a reseeded collection with no cause in a story; LibreChat's writes in journeys/demand.json carry fresh ObjectIds and none is shown repeating a unique value.
rulings.correction: Keep at most one duplicate-key refusal, with its cause shown (a second sign-up with an email already registered, under users' unique email index); delete the rest.

rulings.barItem: content that does not bear out the step's name
rulings.reason: Step 1 is named 'The application's driver asks the server what it is' and sends {hello: 1}. In the driver of record, spec/clients/mongodb-6.20.0.tgz (MongoDB's Node driver 6.20.0, Apache-2.0, the spec's stand-in for the vendor's documentation per spec/SOURCE.md), src/cmap/connect.ts:228-229 the first handshake is the legacy form, {ismaster: 1, helloOk: true, client: {...}}, unless serverApi or loadBalanced is set (LibreChat sets neither); the outline's act 1 itself says 'first in the legacy form'. The legacy answer carries ismaster: true, not the isWritablePrimary the step expects.
rulings.correction: Send step 1 as the driver does, {ismaster: 1, helloOk: true, client: <the driver's metadata document>} on admin, and expect ismaster: true, helloOk: true and maxWireVersion 21.

rulings.barItem: vendor behaviour the vendor's documentation contradicts
rulings.reason: Steps 6-7 have the application insert a document with no _id and read back one the server made. In the driver of record, spec/clients/mongodb-6.20.0.tgz (MongoDB's Node driver 6.20.0, Apache-2.0, the spec's stand-in for the vendor's documentation per spec/SOURCE.md), src/utils.ts:1355-1369 (maybeAddIdToDocuments) sets _id on the client for any document lacking one (forceServerObjectId defaults to false), and mongoose assigns _id on construction; LibreChat never sends a document without _id.
rulings.correction: Delete steps 6-7; LibreChat's inserts carry the ObjectId the driver made.

rulings.barItem: a stated cause that never happens
rulings.reason: Step 201 is 'the refusal LibreChat's probe meets', but journeys/demand.json ('measured') says no command of either reading carried a transaction, and the outline itself puts the only transaction (the MCP authority read) out of this life.

rulings.barItem: a name or id used after it is gone
rulings.reason: Step 197 ends the session whose lsid is AAAAAAAAQACAAAAAAAAAAA== (endSessions, 'as a driver sends on close'), and step 201 then sends a command under that same lsid. The driver returns an ended session to no command (src/sessions.ts, ClientSession over ServerSessionPool); a closed client sends nothing after endSessions.
rulings.correction: Send endSessions only as the last step of the life, when the application closes, with the lsid its commands used; nothing follows under that id.

rulings.reason: Steps 177 and 191 insert five documents into things and the command after each asks of the collection nobody; steps 196 and 198 insert into things in ask_end_sessions and ask_ping and the command after each goes to admin. Each setup is made for an ask that never reads it.

rulings.why: Rewrite the life as the outline's acts in one database on LibreChat's own collections and documents (the commands of journeys/demand.json in its phases: boot, register, login, first page, chat, conversation list and reopen, logout), and correct 'about' to say what the life is.
Keep each command only where the story's act sends it, with the filter, update and options LibreChat sends there; delete the per-option probes.
Delete these read-backs; a read stays only where the application reads in the story (a sign-in finding the user, the conversation list, a conversation reopened).
Keep at most one duplicate-key refusal, with its cause shown (a second sign-up with an email already registered, under users' unique email index); delete the rest.
Send step 1 as the driver does, {ismaster: 1, helloOk: true, client: <the driver's metadata document>} on admin, and expect ismaster: true, helloOk: true and maxWireVersion 21.
Delete steps 6-7; LibreChat's inserts carry the ObjectId the driver made.
Send endSessions only as the last step of the life, when the application closes, with the lsid its commands used; nothing follows under that id.

applied.how: The life is rewritten as the outline's LibreChat story in its own database: 47 commands of its models recorded in order from mongod 7.0.16 (spec/recordings/librechat-story.json), the driver's ismaster+helloOk handshake first and endSessions last; the throwaway-database probes, read-backs, uncaused refusals, no-_id inserts, transaction probe and unused setup are gone, and one E11000 remains, a second sign-up's.
